name: 1 · spec-review.md — is a REQ (or story) buildable, complete, consistent

items.title: All findings in one pass
items.rule: Report every finding the rubric produces in one review round; a finding first raised in round N+1 on unchanged text is a reviewer miss.
items.source: mattpocock `R/mattpocock-skills/skills/productivity/grilling/SKILL.md:8` ("Ask the whole frontier in one round"); ours: fleet self-reports `00-fleet-self-reports.md` spec-reviewer row — #576 took 3 rounds, analyst row #576 4 gaps one per round.
items.recommend: adopt — the most-repeated fleet failure on this axis; cheap to state.

items.title: Every existing-behaviour claim is verified at HEAD
items.rule: Each sentence in a REQ asserting how the system behaves today must cite `file:line` on `origin/master`; the reviewer opens each cite; an unverified claim is a finding.
items.source: humanlayer `R/humanlayer-humanlayer/.claude/commands/create_plan.md:68-72` ("Cross-reference the ticket requirements with actual code"); `research_codebase.md:16` ("ONLY describe what exists"); ours: fleet analyst row #585 (build-cache claim unverified), spec-reviewer row "unverified existing-behaviour claims". Generalises `SR/:215-220` C-09, which today fires only on "no impact" claims.
items.kind: review check (new criterion C-11, BLOCKER when the claim is false, GAP when uncited).
items.recommend: adopt — C-09 already proves the pattern; this widens it to every factual claim.

items.title: Cites are re-checked against current master
items.rule: A `file:NN` cite in a REQ or issue body that no longer points at the named symbol is a finding; the check is mechanical, not reviewer memory.
items.source: ours #61 row 15 (#636 "`file:NN` cites in stories unchecked"); fleet spec-reviewer row "line drift vs HEAD"; `W/scripts/check-doc-drift.sh:94` §2 already checks file:line citations but only over AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, `docs/architecture`, `.claude/rules` (`W/Makefile:357`).
items.kind: mechanical → extend `check-doc-drift.sh` §2 to `docs/spec/REQ-*.md` and (via `glab`) the issue body.
items.recommend: adopt — the script exists; scope is a path list change. Note `SR/:321` (anchor findings to headings) stays.

items.title: No open question survives approval
items.rule: Before `/approved`, the REQ's open-questions list is empty or each item names who decides it and why it does not block building.
items.source: humanlayer `create_plan.md:338-343` ("Do NOT write the plan with unresolved questions"); keeps `SR/:39-41` rule 1 intact (reviewer surfaces, never answers).
items.recommend: adopt — closes the gap between "surface it" and the gate.

items.title: A spec does not contradict decided work
items.rule: Grep closed issues, accepted ADRs and merged REQs on the same subject; a REQ reversing a decision without naming it is a BLOCKER.
items.source: ours fleet analyst row (D-F8 vs #533 — contradicted decided work); extends `SR/:130-135` A-03 (ADRs only) to decided issues/REQs.
items.recommend: hold — needs one agreed place where "decided" lives (issue label or decision log) before it is checkable.

items.title: Story pre-check lives here too
items.rule: A story is checked for actor/action/benefit, checkable scenarios, an out-of-scope list, and an Escalation answer (migration, security, cross-module → full REQ).
items.source: ours `W/docs/agents/personas/spec-reviewer.md:20-24`, `analyst.md:46-47`; fleet spec-reviewer row "missing Escalation sections"; disposition `14-disposition-table.md:177` (checklists → spec-review.md).
items.kind: review check (new short group S, story tier).
items.recommend: adopt — the persona split deletes its only home.

items.title: One change-class gate, stated positively
items.rule: Decide the review tier from what the diff **is** (code · operability · authority doc · process/docs); an unplaceable path is code.
items.source: `AR/:49-60` rule 4 (positive class table, "When you cannot place a path, it is code"); replaces `SR/:52-66` rule 5, which is stated as what the diff is not.
items.recommend: adopt — two tier gates with different wording drift; AR's form is the safer one.

items.title: Scenarios cover state that existed before the change
items.rule: When a change alters stored data or a default, at least one scenario's Given is state created before the change (old row, unseeded key).
items.source: ours `14-disposition-table.md:114` (P1:9 "AC-6 proved only on new rows"); fleet qa row "ACs asserting defaults not behaviour"; `SR/MEMORY.md:9-13` (un-defaulted reader).
items.recommend: adopt — the one AC gap with two independent fleet incidents.

items.title: Prune columns that never vary
items.rule: An Examples column whose value is identical on every row moves to Background or the Given; it is not a placeholder.
items.source: today `W/.agents/skills/planning/references/acceptance-criteria.md:56-72` (rule 3); not covered by GA4 (which fixes header↔placeholder match only).
items.recommend: adopt — the only one of today's four rules GA1–GA6 do not already carry.

items.title: Domain words only
items.rule: Scenario text uses terms from the glossary and sibling REQs; a new noun is declared in the REQ before a scenario uses it.
items.source: mattpocock `R/mattpocock-skills/skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md:13` ("Use the project's domain glossary vocabulary"); `SR/:137-142` A-04.
items.recommend: adopt — GT1 makes the title the test name, so a bad word lands in code.

items.title: Changing an approved AC re-opens approval
items.rule: Editing the text of an AC after `/approved` (not only its id) is a spec change: record it on the MR and get a fresh `/approved`.
items.source: ours `W/.agents/skills/crq/SKILL.md:250` (approval covers the design as it stood); extends GA2 (ids only).
items.recommend: adopt — GA2 freezes the id, nothing freezes the meaning.

items.title: Manual-only checks are labelled
items.rule: A criterion no IT or smoke can assert is marked `# manual` with the exact human step; it never sits unmarked among automated scenarios.
items.source: humanlayer `create_plan.md:345-359` (automated vs manual verification); AT1 (`19-approved-rules.md:31`).
items.recommend: hold — AT1 says every AC is proven by IT or smoke; operator should decide whether manual ACs are allowed at all.

items.title: Call-tree diff for control-flow changes
items.rule: A design that adds or reroutes a call path shows the call tree as a fenced `diff`, `+` for new calls, `-` for removed.
items.source: ACE `wsff.md:491` ("Call-stack trees, for any orchestration or control-flow change"); `:536` (cheaper than deciding in code review).
items.recommend: adopt.

items.title: File-tree diff with test files
items.rule: The design shows a file-tree diff marking every new, modified and deleted file, test files included, each with a one-line purpose.
items.source: ACE `wsff.md:507-515` (`# NEW` / `# MODIFIED` annotations); humanlayer `create_plan.md:215-219` (File / Changes per component).
items.recommend: adopt — also the input F-01 grades against.

items.title: Types and signatures, bodies left out
items.rule: New records, sealed interfaces, ports and public method signatures are written in Java with no bodies; usage by the caller is written first.
items.source: ACE `wsff.md:517` ("too internal for an architecture doc but that an agent might still get wrong"); pstack `R/cursor-plugins/pstack/skills/architect/SKILL.md:9,83` ("caller's usage is written first").
items.recommend: adopt.

items.title: Thin end-to-end slices, not stack order
items.rule: The build order is slices that each run end-to-end and can be poked (curl, UI, IT); never migration → service → API → UI as separate steps.
items.source: ACE `wsff.md:542-566` ("Models love what I call 'horizontal plans'"); mattpocock `to-tickets/SKILL.md:31-34`; addy `planning-and-task-breakdown/SKILL.md:57-77`.
items.recommend: adopt — direct fix for review-time discovery (!230).

items.title: Each slice names its check as a make command
items.rule: Every slice states the `make` target (and `TEST=` filter) that proves it, plus any manual step.
items.source: humanlayer `create_plan.md:225-232,325` ("automated steps should use `make` whenever possible"); ours AGENTS.md make-front-door block.
items.recommend: adopt.

items.title: Program design lives beside the REQ, not in it
items.rule: Paths, signatures and trees go in the draft MR's design section (or `docs/design/`), never in the REQ, which stays behaviour-only.
items.source: mattpocock `to-spec/SKILL.md:55` ("Do NOT include specific file paths or code snippets"); ours SR3 (cites rot).
items.recommend: adopt — keeps the REQ stable after merge while the design is disposable.

items.title: Deviation from the sketch is surfaced
items.rule: During stage 6, a needed change to an approved type, signature or file placement is posted on the MR before coding past it.
items.source: pstack `architect/SKILL.md:57` ("Deviations from the sketch are signal worth surfacing"); `AR/:348-353` F-01.
items.recommend: adopt — gives F-01 a recorded baseline instead of a guess.

items.title: Two shapes before one, for a new seam
items.rule: A new module, port or cross-module contract is sketched in two structurally different shapes before one is chosen; the rejected shape gets one line.
items.source: pstack `architect/SKILL.md:35` ("Design it twice"); mattpocock `codebase-design/DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md:3`.
items.recommend: hold — real cost per design; limit to new seams only if adopted.

items.title: Mermaid in committed docs, ASCII in replies
items.rule: A diagram committed to a `.md` file is a ```` ```mermaid ```` fence; a diagram in chat, Discord or an MR comment is plain fenced ASCII.
items.source: today `diagrams.md:3-12`; ND-10 default (`14-disposition-table.md:261`); R1:90 contradiction noted at `:120`.
items.recommend: adopt — settles the recorded contradiction.

items.title: Program-design trees are `diff` fences, not Mermaid
items.rule: Call trees and file trees in a design use fenced `diff` text; Mermaid is for component, sequence, state, ER and class diagrams.
items.source: ACE `wsff.md:479` ("Mermaid ... lure you into a false sense that you are aligned"), `:487-489`.
items.recommend: adopt — keeps DG1 and PD1–PD2 consistent.

items.title: Node labels are real, greppable names
items.rule: Every node label is a class, module, table or endpoint name that `grep` finds on master.
items.source: today `diagrams.md:31-32`.
items.kind: mechanical → add Mermaid node labels to `check-doc-drift.sh` §4 named symbols (`:147`).
items.recommend: adopt as reference rule now; mechanical check hold until §4 scope is widened (SR3 same change).

items.title: One diagram, one question
items.rule: Each diagram answers one question from the type table; a second question gets a second diagram.
items.source: today `diagrams.md:16-25,29-30`.
items.recommend: adopt (keep).

items.title: A diagram that needs a paragraph is redrawn
items.rule: If understanding the diagram requires prose beyond a one-line caption, redraw it smaller rather than adding text.
items.source: mattpocock `R/mattpocock-skills/skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/HTML-REPORT.md:55` ("If the diagram needs a paragraph to be understood, redraw the diagram").
items.recommend: adopt — matches the operator's show-me style.

items.title: A diagram lives in the doc it explains
items.rule: Put the diagram in the ADR, REQ or design doc it illustrates; no standalone diagrams file.
items.source: today `diagrams.md:33-34`.
items.recommend: adopt (keep).

items.title: No trust stamps
items.rule: Do not write `[confirmed: …]` or any in-text verification marker; a claim that needs proof gets a cite the drift check can run.
items.source: `W/AGENTS.md:432-437`; ours #335 (65 stamps, 3 sampled all defective), REQ-069.
items.kind: MUST (L2) — short enough to stay always-on.
items.recommend: adopt.

items.title: Name the thing, not the tally
items.rule: Do not write counts that change as a side effect of unrelated work; stable deliberate facts (Java 25, port 8080, a TTL) are fine.
items.source: `W/AGENTS.md:439-441`; `W/scripts/check-doc-drift.sh:3-7` (PUBLIC_PATHS 17→20, 57→58 controllers).
items.recommend: adopt — and wire `make doc-drift` into `make lint` (today it runs only on its own target, `W/Makefile:359-360`, not in `verify` `:379`).

items.title: Known-stale claims go in Doc drift
items.rule: A claim known to disagree with the code is recorded in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §9 Doc drift, never fixed with a bracket or left silent.
items.source: `W/AGENTS.md:444`; `W/docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:609`.
items.recommend: adopt.

items.title: Uncomfortable operational truths go in
items.rule: Write the operational fact even when it is unflattering; a reassuring false line is the worst line a doc can carry.
items.source: `W/AGENTS.md:442-443` (only-the-api-runs-migrations line).
items.recommend: adopt.

items.title: REQ only for new behaviour
items.rule: A bug corrects the REQ it violates, in place; a chore with no owning REQ carries problem, scope and ACs in the issue; a new REQ is for behaviour the product lacks.
items.source: `W/AGENTS.md:446-449`.
items.recommend: adopt.

items.title: REQ number = issue number; ADR number cross-branch
items.rule: A new REQ is `REQ-<issue>-slug`; a new ADR takes the next number free on master and every in-flight branch, per `docs/adr/README.md`.
items.source: `W/AGENTS.md:449-453`; `W/docs/adr/README.md:26,59`; evidence: two `REQ-073-*` files exist on this branch (`docs/spec/REQ-073-jacoco-integration-coverage.md`, `REQ-073-tool-rename-name-uniqueness.md`). Rejects mattpocock `domain-modeling/ADR-FORMAT.md:27` ("Scan `docs/adr/` for the highest existing number") — that is the collision we hit.
items.kind: mechanical → extend `check-migration-version.sh`-style cross-branch hook to `docs/adr/`; REQ side is a reference rule.
items.recommend: adopt — and note the vendored ADR-FORMAT must carry our override (disposition :125).

items.title: One owner per fact
items.rule: Each fact lives in one file; other docs link to it rather than restate it, and generated docs are never hand-edited.
items.source: mattpocock `writing-for-agents/SKILL.md:78` (single source of truth); kunchenguid-firstmate `AGENTS.md:55` ("single owner of the top-level ... layout"); openclaw `docs/AGENTS.md:38` ("Generated docs, never hand-edit").
items.recommend: adopt — it is the principle the whole one-rulebook move rests on.

items.title: Do not restate what the environment answers
items.rule: Do not copy into docs what one command or file answers (make targets, versions in build files); write the why and the gotcha instead.
items.source: mattpocock `writing-for-agents/SKILL.md:79` ("a document that restates it is a cache").
items.recommend: hold — overlaps WD2/WD7; adopt only if the operator wants the "cache" word as a leading term.
